title: Microprobe Signal Stitching Playbook
body:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook captures a compact approach to putting small, repeatable synthetic probes (microprobes) into service as first-class observability signals for inference. The goal is to provide a stitched signal set that maps a probe -> metric -> trace anchor -> dashboard tile, and to define a lightweight gating checklist so product/ops can reliably decide when a rollout or rollback is required.

Why microprobes?
- Fast actionable feedback: small, deterministic probes that exercise critical code paths (kv warm, prefix cache, batching edge cases, quantized kernels) provide high SNR for regressions.
- Low cost and deterministic coverage: probes run at controlled cadence and are designed to be stable across regions and model variants.
- Traceability: each probe execution carries a structured trace id and tags to make trace anchoring trivial for SRE/ops.

Probe taxonomy (high level):
- Warm-Start KV Probe: synthetic request with long prefix to validate KV cache hit ratio and tail latency under light concurrency.
- Cold-Start Model Probe: new model container spin-up and first-token latency.
- Quantization Smoke Probe: short sequence that hits quantized execution path and validates numerical sanity and latency.
- Multi-model Fanout Probe: single request that fans out to routing policy variants and measures aggregation latency & error.
- Rate-limit Boundary Probe: burst of small requests to validate throttling and graceful degradation.

Core metric definitions (canonical names, unit, short description):
- probe.kv_warm.latency.p50_ms: milliseconds, median latency for warm-start KV probe response time.
- probe.kv_warm.kv_hit_ratio: ratio [0-1], fraction of requests served from KV cache for the probe set.
- probe.cold_start.first_token_ms: ms, time until first token emitted for cold-start probe.
- probe.quant_smoke.numeric-diff_l1: float, L1 difference of token logits or normalized output against golden baseline.
- probe.fanout.aggregate_95th_ms: ms, 95th percentile of aggregate latency across fanout legs.
- probe.ratelimit.rejection_rate: fraction, percent of probe requests rejected due to rate limit in window.

Tracing anchors and spans:
- Each probe execution must attach trace tags: probe.name, probe.run_id, model.variant, region, container_id.
- Span taxonomy: probe-root -> http-call -> model-inference -> kv-lookup (optional) -> kernel-launch.
- Sampling: all microprobe traces are sampled at 100% for the first 24 hours after a probe regression, then downsampled to 5% for long-term retention.
- Trace enrichment: attach the probe input hash and golden-output-hash to span attributes for quick binary comparisons in trace UI.

Dashboard mapping and stitching rules:
- Rule: every probe metric has a one-click trace anchor from the dashboard tile (tile-level link to trace filter probe.run_id).
- Tile composition: small panel (single metric sparkline), adjacent heatmap for latency distribution, and a compact table showing recent trace links (last 10 runs).
- Cross-correlation row: show kv_hit_ratio vs p95 latency in same panel using dual axis; label anomalies when ratio drops > 5% and p95 increases > 20% in the same window.

Gating checklist for rollouts (canary -> global):
1) Baseline stability: microprobe baseline must be within delta thresholds for 48h on canary traffic.
2) No traceable numerics regressions: quant_smoke.numeric-diff_l1 < 0.02 across sample set.
3) Resource signals stable: container CPU/GPU utilization allowed delta < 10% and memory stable.
4) Latency SLI: probe.*.p95 and p99 must be within alerted thresholds; no sustained p99 increases.
5) Operator go/no-go sign-off: SRE and Product must mark "pass" in rollout board.

Alerting playbook (short):
- Alert type: Probe regression
- Trigger: any of: kv_hit_ratio drop > 10% vs baseline OR probe.kv_warm.p95 > baseline *1.3 OR quant_smoke.numeric-diff_l1 > threshold
- Severity mapping: severity=critical if p99 increases >50% AND rejection_rate >5%
- First responder: oncall-observability channel + runbook link.
- Automated remediation steps: throttle traffic to lower tier, route to fallback model variant, warm caches, and trigger model rollback if numeric regression persists >1 hour.

Cadence and operational cost constraints:
- Default probe cadence: 1 probe per minute across regions for warm/cold probes; quantization and fanout runs once every 5 minutes.
- Storage and trace costs: projections show 300 probes/day per region yields ~5k traces/month; cap at 5 regions for default. Adjust cadence per model criticality.

Instrumentation checklist for engineers (developer facing):
- Add probe.name and probe.run_id to request headers and propagate to trace context.
- Emit the canonical metric names as counters/gauges and add tag dimensions: model.version, variant, region, tenancy (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Ensure probe payloads are deterministic and small; store golden baselines in config repo with versioned ids.

Investigation workflow (operator):
1) Observe metric delta in dashboard -> click trace anchor -> inspect kv-lookup spans for cache miss patterns.
2) If numeric regression, run diff runner: pull last 20 probe outputs and compare to golden baselines; surface token-level diffs.
3) If model-level issue, escalate to applied-ml and attach trace + sample payload.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- Probe signal brittleness: how often to refresh golden baselines for model drift vs noise? (proposal: automated golden-refresh weekly with manual review).
- Sampling policy for long-term trace retention to balance cost and reproducibility.
- Multi-tenant tagging semantics: keep tenant ids hashed in traces to avoid PII leakage.

Immediate TODOs:
- (Marco) Define golden-baseline storage layout in repo and add README.
- (Priya) Wire dashboard tiles with trace-link buttons and heatmap panel.
- (Ethan) Add 100% sampling for probe traces during next release window.
- (Aisha) Draft runbook for automated fallback routing when kv_hit_ratio drops below threshold.

Appendix: quick metric guardrails (recommended deltas)
- kv_hit_ratio: alert if delta <= -0.10 vs baseline
- probe.kv_warm.p95: alert if > baseline * 1.3
- quant_smoke.numeric-diff_l1: alert if > 0.02 (investigate if > 0.05)

Notes to self: keep microprobes lightweight and focused. These should reduce noise for SREs and create deterministic probes that stitch into the broader observability signal set. Next meeting: 2026-02-24 to sign off on gating thresholds and cadence for canary groups.
